confirmed.title: SKILL.md Step 8 documents a template variable set that cannot render the actual gsc-pull report template
confirmed.description: Step 8 (render_report) tells the operator to call `render_template.py templates/reports/gsc-pull.template.md data.json` and lists the substitution variables as $project_slug, $date, $days_back, $total_urls, $top_rising_url, $top_rising_delta_pct, $top_decay_url, $top_decay_delta_pct, $report_summary. But the ACTUAL template file templates/reports/gsc-pull.template.md requires a near-disjoint set: $project_slug, $date, $days_back, $row_count_recent, $row_count_previous, $unique_urls, $top_5_pages, $delta_summary, $run_id, $rows_written. Only 3 of the 9 documented variables ($project_slug, $date, $days_back) actually appear in the template; the other 6 ($total_urls, $top_rising_url, $top_rising_delta_pct, $top_decay_url, $top_decay_delta_pct, $report_summary) do not exist in the template at all, and 7 template variables the renderer DEMANDS are undocumented in the SKILL.md. This is load-bearing: scripts/reporting/render_template.py:53-55 calls Template(...).substitute(...) which raises KeyError and exits 1 (`_die(f"missing key in data: {exc.args[0]}")`) on ANY $token present in the template but absent from the data dict. An operator who builds data.json from the SKILL.md's documented variable list would therefore get a hard 'missing key in data: row_count_recent' failure and could never render outputs/reports/{date}-gsc-pull.md. The documented Step 8 procedure is impossible to execute against the shipped template.

The finding's load-bearing legal premise is FALSE. (1) There is NO cross-sheet invariant tying allowed_writers to completed_work. F-01 is literally "master_task.status ⊆ statusEnum" — unrelated. Zero of the 31 rules reference allowed_writers at all. So the claim "per F-1 schema authority NO skill may append to completed_work" and "if implemented it would breach F-1" is fabricated; the high severity rests entirely on this non-existent rule. (2) completed_work.allowed_writers is ABSENT in the schema, not null — allowed_writers is declared for master_task ONLY (line 318). The finder's "verified: allowed_writers: None" is a Python dict.get on a missing key. Per the project's documented decision (OPEN_QUESTIONS.md:635 "Option d accepted"), absent allowed_writers means transaction._check_writer_scope BYPASSES the gate — writes are PERMITTED (provenance via events.jsonl). (3) completed_work is in fact a writable sheet, owned by the mark-done skill (design spec 1058 "completed_work | mark-done"; mark-done SKILL.md:71-73 appends the row via writer_id done_protocol; PHASE_STATUS.md:218 documents it in production). verify-indexing's "allowed_writers=null" line is its own per-skill read-only stance, carefully qualified "(effectively; schema declares no writer field)" — NOT a global prohibition the finder portrays it as.

Through the intentional-design lens, the R-121 section is an explicit spec lock with runtime DEFERRED to Phase 11 Wave 2 (lines 239-242: "scripts/production/new_blog.py does not yet exist") and is a faithful transcription of the approved compliance-audit plan (plan line 1461: "atomic with completed_work row append"). The prose at 227-232 is passive ("the completed_work row ... also records"; "reads from this same completed_work log ... single source of truth") and describes reading the mark-done-owned completed_work SSoT, not new-blog performing the write. Step 12 emit_provenance writes only events.jsonl; the body contains no transaction.append/update/delete token, so the READ-ONLY-w.r.t.-master.xlsx claim and the test guard both hold.

The only genuine residual is a cosmetic wording imprecision: the phrase "atomic with the events.jsonl audit append in Step 12" loosely narrates a mark-done-owned completed_work append inside new-blog's Step 12, which could read tighter. That is a doc-polish nit far below "high," does not contradict the never-calls-transaction promise, and breaches no invariant. Net: severity is inflated on a false premise, the behavior is a deliberately-deferred, plan-sanctioned spec lock, and there is no new, unaddressed contract violation. real=false.

So the finding's severity-justifying F-1/schema-null sub-argument is overstated, but its PRIMARY thesis (internal contradiction of the skill's own READ-ONLY/"only mutation is events.jsonl" claim, undeclared in outputs/produces, uncaught by the grep guard) stands on independent re-reading. ONE INACCURACY in the finding's reasoning chain: it claims schemas/master-excel.schema.json "sets sheets.completed_work.allowed_writers = null" and infers "per F-1 NO skill may append." confirmed.title: events.jsonl event_kind declared as `production` — invalid against the F-8 events schema it cites (content_revise must be event_kind=work)
confirmed.description: Step 8 documents the events.jsonl append envelope as the skill's output contract (F-8). Line 407 declares `event_kind = production`. NOTE: the paired test's Test 9 (test_events_event_type_content_revise, lines 161-169) asserts event_type==content_revise and that events.jsonl is in outputs, but never asserts event_kind — which is exactly why this schema-invalid value passes the paired test.

confirmed.title: Headline capabilities (drift-via-events, GSC 5σ anomaly, budget burn) are documented as active but the inline implementation stubs them as 'Phase 14+ scope' and reads entirely different sources
confirmed.description: The frontmatter description (lines 6-9), Workflow steps 2/4/5 (lines 195-207), DURUR #3/#5 (lines 168-189), and Principle 1 (lines 430-435) all present three capabilities as ACTIVE and truth-verifiable: (a) drift reuse by filtering events.jsonl on event_kind=audit AND audit_target=invariants:*; (b) GSC week-over-week 5σ anomaly detection by reading master.xlsx[gsc_performance] via openpyxl read_only; (c) budget burn rate by aggregating events.jsonl cost.credits per day vs budget_credits_per_day. But the ONLY runtime (inline Blocks 1-3, lines 227-406) does NONE of these: Block 1 reads _state/cache/consistency-report.json (not the events.jsonl invariants filter), Block 2 reads shared/portfolio.json, and Blocks never open master.xlsx, never import openpyxl, never read events.jsonl, and never aggregate cost.credits. The gsc_anomaly_section, budget_burn_section, and escalations are hard-coded placeholder strings that literally announce the real logic is deferred ('Phase 14+ governance refinement scope', 'Budget burn rate calc Phase 14+ scope', 'DURUR #5 5σ anomaly threshold check Phase 14+ governance scope'). The frontmatter status:active (line 25) plus the un-caveated description/Workflow/DURUR present these as shipped, so an operator reading the contract is misled into believing a 5σ GSC alarm and budget-burn alarm fire when in fact neither is computed. The deferral is honest only inside Block 3; it is NOT surfaced in the frontmatter/Workflow/DURUR that an operator reads first.

confirmed.title: build_report_markdown uses safe_substitute but documents render_template.py compatibility and catches a KeyError that can never fire (dead branch)
confirmed.description: SKILL.md (L102-103, L221, body L440 docstring) states the report is rendered 'via string.Template per scripts/reporting/render_template.py convention' / 'render_template.py compatible'. The convention module render_template.py uses Template(...).substitute() which RAISES KeyError on an unknown $key. portfolio_overview.build_report_markdown instead calls .safe_substitute(), which never raises on unknown/missing keys (it leaves them verbatim). The function then wraps the call in 'except KeyError ... raise PortfolioOverviewError(...)', but safe_substitute cannot raise KeyError, so that except branch is dead code. This is a minor behavioral divergence from the cited convention (strict vs lenient substitution) plus an unreachable error path that misrepresents the failure mode.
confirmed.evidence: portfolio_overview.py L454 'return Template(template_text).safe_substitute(' followed by L457-460 'except KeyError as exc: raise PortfolioOverviewError(f"template substitution failed - missing key: {exc.args[0]}")'. Convention render_template.py L: 'rendered = Template(template_text).substitute({k: str(v) for k, v in data.items()})' (strict, raises KeyError). SKILL.md L440 docstring claims 'render_template.py compatible'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either switch to .substitute() to truly match the render_template.py convention and keep the KeyError guard meaningful, or keep safe_substitute and remove the dead except KeyError branch plus reword the SKILL.md claim to 'string.Template safe_substitute (lenient)' so the documented behavior matches the code.

Re-read all cited files. CONFIRMED verbatim: (1) skills/reporting/portfolio-overview/SKILL.md L102-103 "rendered via `string.Template` per `scripts/reporting/render_template.py` convention" (also L221-222 "string.Template $var rendering convention"); (2) scripts/reporting/portfolio_overview.py docstring L440-441 "render_template.py compatible"; (3) render_template.py L53 uses strict `Template(...).substitute({...})` which raises KeyError on unknown $key; (4) portfolio_overview.py L454 uses `.safe_substitute(...)` and L457-460 wraps it in `except KeyError as exc: raise PortfolioOverviewError(f"template substitution failed - missing key: {exc.args[0]}")`.

EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED with python3: `string.Template.safe_substitute` never raises KeyError for unknown/missing placeholders — it leaves them verbatim ('$unknown' stays). Only strict `.substitute()` raises. Therefore the `except KeyError` branch at L457-460 is provably unreachable DEAD CODE, and a missing $key silently leaks "$placeholder" text into the published report instead of raising the advertised PortfolioOverviewError.

UNADDRESSED: grep across tests/ shows NO test references `safe_substitute` or "substitution failed"; the only paired test (tests/skills/test_portfolio_overview.py Test 8, L334-373) is a happy-path render smoke that never exercises the error branch nor asserts strict-vs-lenient behavior. The existing guards in scope (status-parity, trigger-parity) do not touch this. content_validator is out of scope and unrelated.

This is a genuine 6-io-drift: the doc promises render_template.py-convention behavior (strict, raises on missing key) but the code uses lenient safe_substitute AND keeps an unreachable error path that misrepresents the failure mode. Severity "low" is appropriate (fixed in-repo template makes the unknown-key path unlikely in practice; the dialect/$var family IS shared). Counter-argument considered: one could read "convention/compatible" as referring only to the $variable dialect, not the error policy — but the dead `except KeyError` branch is an objective, independent code defect regardless of that reading, so the finding holds. Minor evidence-field slip (labeling the docstring as "SKILL.md L440" when it is portfolio_overview.py L440) is a cross-reference error, not a fabricated/misattributed quote — the description body correctly attributes it to "body L440 docstring" and the quoted text genuinely exists there; does not undermine the finding. Suggested fix is correct.

Independently substantiated against the actual files. (1) scripts/reporting/portfolio_overview.py L454 calls Template(template_text).safe_substitute(...), wrapped in except KeyError (L457-460). (2) The cited convention scripts/reporting/render_template.py L53 uses Template(...).substitute(...) — strict, raises KeyError on unknown $key. (3) SKILL.md asserts the render_template.py convention in five places (L102-103 'rendered via string.Template per render_template.py convention', L142, L221-222, L242-243, plus docstring L440-441 'render_template.py compatible'). So the code (lenient safe_substitute) genuinely diverges from its documented convention (strict substitute). (4) Python stdlib semantics: safe_substitute never raises KeyError, so the except KeyError branch is unreachable — confirmed dead path whose 'missing key' message misrepresents the real failure mode.

Crucially the divergence is NOT cosmetic, and the two defects mask each other: the template templates/reports/portfolio-overview.template.md references $run_id (L35 in the 'Kanıt zinciri' evidence section, and a 'Run ID:' line), but the data dict in build_report_markdown (L443-452) has NO run_id key (grep run_id on the file returns zero matches). Therefore under the DOCUMENTED strict .substitute() this template would raise KeyError('run_id') and the guard WOULD fire — the except branch is dead only because safe_substitute was used. Under the actual safe_substitute, the literal string '$run_id' is silently emitted into the published report's provenance/evidence chain. The paired test tests/skills/test_portfolio_overview.py::test_template_render_smoke (L334-373) only asserts section headers and never asserts absence of unsubstituted '$' tokens or exercises run_id, so the leak ships unnoticed. The finder's claim that the missing-key path 'can never fire' is actually an understatement of the problem (it provably fires under the documented convention), but every load-bearing fact checks out.

GUARD-AWARE / NOVELTY lens: not covered by test_status_declaration_parity.py (status, unrelated) or test_trigger_declaration_parity.py (triggers, unrelated); not in the 8-skill active->wip set (3ddd13c); not indexing-ping; not content_validator.py; does not touch the Indexing-API-consent or AI-disclosure hard rules. The render_template.py-referenced test_template_dialect.py only governs dialect-family ownership (string.Template vs {{PLACEHOLDER}}), not strict-vs-lenient semantics, and does not cover portfolio_overview.build_report_markdown — so this IO-drift is genuinely unguarded and unaddressed. Verdict: real.
